T01: Hi, I'm JR. Let's get Grok ready on your computer. Open your web browser and go to grok dot com. There's nothing to download. Tap Sign up, or Sign in if you already have an account, and use your email, Google, or your X account. You only ever type your password on Grok's own page, so never give it to anyone.
T02: You never have to type in this training. On your phone keyboard, tap the little microphone and just talk. Say what you want, the same way you'd text a friend. Try it now, then tap I did it.
T03: Tap the button on this screen to open Grok's website. It opens in a new tab. When you see the sign-in page, come back here and tap I did it.
T04: If you use Google, tap the Google button. If you have an X account, you can use that. Or type your email and follow the steps. If it asks for a password, you make it yourself, on Grok's page only.
T05: If you signed up with your email, open your inbox and look for the message from Grok. Use the code or the link inside it. If you used Google or X, skip this one.
T06: Answer the last few questions on the screen. You're done when you see an empty message box waiting for you.
T07: On your phone, open the App Store on an iPhone, or Google Play on Android. Search for Grok. Make sure it's the official Grok app, with the same icon you see on this screen, then tap Get or Install. It's free.
T08: Open the Grok app and sign in the same way you just did. When you see the same empty message box, you're set.
T09: Now let's talk to it. Tap the message box, tap the microphone, and read the message on this screen out loud. Or tap Copy and paste it in. Then send it.
T10: Grok will ask you a few questions about your business, one at a time. Just answer like you're texting. Short answers are fine.
T11: If you don't love an answer, just say so. Try saying, make that shorter. Grok rewrites it. You're always in charge.
T12: Grok can't see your business, so tell it. Say who you are, what a good answer looks like, give an example if you have one, and end with: ask me anything you need to know first.
T13: Let's try it on something real. Copy the request on this screen, change the parts in brackets to your own details, and send it. You'll get an email draft you can actually use.
T14: Grok can read pictures. In the app, tap the button to add a photo, take a picture of a receipt or a note, and ask it to type out what's on it.
T15: Let's teach Grok who you are, one time. Look for the setting called Customize Grok. Paste in the note on this screen, fill in your details, and save. Now Grok knows who you are in your chats.
T16: Here's one you'll use every week. Copy this request, paste in a real customer email at the end, and send. Read the reply once before you send it to your customer.
T17: Copy this request, fill in what you need to get done and your appointments, and send it. Grok builds you a simple plan for the week.
T18: Grok is helpful, but it can be wrong. After any important answer, ask: which parts are you least sure about? And always read anything before it goes to a customer, a bank, or the government.
T19: Never put passwords, card numbers, bank numbers, or Social Security numbers into Grok, or any chat. If you need help with something private, swap the names and numbers for something like Customer A.
T20: Everything you just did works on Grok's free plan. The free plan has limits, so if you hit one, take a break and come back later. Only upgrade if a limit keeps costing you time. Great job. You're set up.
